name: ClearCaptions Mobile
oneLine: US phone-call caption app for iPhone and iPad, using speech recognition and sometimes a live captioner, free through the FCC for eligible people with hearing loss.

platforms.detail: The app runs on iPhone and iPad; the App Store also lists Apple silicon Macs and Apple Vision. ClearCaptions' pages name no Android app and none was found on Google Play. Eligible people can also get a free home ClearCaptions Phone.

deviceRequirements.detail: The App Store says iOS 15.0 or later; ClearCaptions' own pages still say iOS 12.0 and list phones up to iPhone 11. You also need Wi-Fi or mobile data and a registered ClearCaptions account.

roomCaptions.detail: ClearCaptions' terms say the app is meant for its captioned telephone service, which captions telephone calls, and only the words of the person on the call are captioned. No ClearCaptions page mentions captions for people in the same room.

groupConversations.detail: You can add a third caller to a call. No ClearCaptions page describes captions for a group in the same room.

languages.detail: ClearCaptions says its captions are currently only in English, and you must be able to communicate in English to qualify. Its terms of use still mention bilingual English/Spanish users.

offline.detail: The app needs Wi-Fi or mobile data to caption calls.

speakerLabels.detail: Only the words of the other person on the call are captioned; nothing is said about labelling speakers on 3-way calls.

translation.detail: No ClearCaptions page describes translation. Captions are in English only.

saveTranscripts.text: Yes, if you choose; on your device
saveTranscripts.detail: If you choose to save them, captions of past calls stay in the app's call log, only on your device. ClearCaptions says it keeps no record of your call log or caption history.

export.detail: No ClearCaptions page describes sharing or exporting saved captions.

fileUpload.detail: No ClearCaptions page mentions transcribing an audio or video file.

summaries.detail: No ClearCaptions page mentions summaries of calls.

customWords.detail: No ClearCaptions page mentions adding your own words or names.

display.detail: You can change the caption font, size and colour in the app. The home ClearCaptions Phone has a large touchscreen with adjustable caption size and colour.

soundAlerts.detail: No alerts for sounds around you are described. The home ClearCaptions Phone has a flashing light for incoming calls and FEMA emergency alerts.

phoneCalls.detail: Captions incoming and outgoing calls, voicemail, 3-way calls and 911 calls. The app gives you a separate ClearCaptions number; forward your mobile number to it to get captions on all incoming calls.

videoCalls.detail: ClearCaptions' FAQ says the ClearCaptions Phone is only for audio calls, and its terms describe the app for telephone calls. No page describes video calls in the app.

mediaOnDevice.detail: No ClearCaptions page describes captioning videos or other audio playing on the device.

humanCaptioners.detail: ClearCaptions uses speech recognition software for most calls and, in some cases, a live communications assistant.

privacy.text: Cloud; calls not kept after the call
privacy.detail: The other person's voice goes to ClearCaptions' captioners and speech recognition. Its terms say neither the audio nor the transcription is kept, except voicemail for home phone users; saved captions stay on your device. The App Store label says the app collects no data.

account.text: Yes; name, DOB, last 4 of SSN
account.detail: You sign up by phone or an online form so ClearCaptions can check you qualify. Registration asks for your full name, date of birth, last four digits of your Social Security number, address and phone number; you self-certify your hearing loss and no doctor's note is needed.

availability.detail: Only for people living in the US and its territories; its terms say the service is for people located in the United States. The app was not found in the UK, Canadian, Mexican, Australian or German App Stores.

freePlan.text: Free, no call limit, for eligible users
freePlan.detail: Free for eligible US residents whose hearing loss requires captions to use the phone: no contracts or fees, and no limit on how many calls you make with captions.

price.detail: The app is free with no in-app purchases on the US App Store (October 2026). An optional second home ClearCaptions Phone can be bought; its price isn't stated.

accessibilityFunding.detail: The FCC lists ClearCaptions, LLC with full certification to provide IP CTS. Calls are paid for from the federal TRS Fund.

strengths.text: Free for eligible US users with no limit on the number of calls, paid from the FCC's TRS Fund.
Captions incoming and outgoing calls, voicemail, 3-way calls and 911 calls on iPhone and iPad.

sources.title: Terms of Use
quotes: Last updated November 6, 2025

The Service provides near real-time call captions of phone conversations for English and Bilingual (English/Spanish) individuals who have hearing loss that necessitates the use of the IP Captioned Telephone Service.

The Service may employ a communications assistant who, with the aid of speech recognition software, converts the other party’s spoken words into captioned text in an otherwise standard voice telephone environment. The Service also may employ speech recognition software alone, without a communications assistant.

“Registration Form” means all the information collected as part of the registration process including, but not limited to, your full legal name, date of birth, last four digits of your social security number, address, and telephone number.
“Endpoints” means a ClearCaptions Phone, ClearCaptions Mobile Application for iPhone, iPad, android and tablet and/or other end-user provided devices used in connection with the Services.
The saved captioning is stored on the Endpoint running the Application. The resulting caption record is accessible to you, but it is not accessible by us.

To protect your privacy, with the exception of voicemail recordings stored on ClearCaptions’ servers for ClearCaptions Phone customers using ClearCaptions Telephone Number to access and retrieve their voicemail messages, neither the audio transmission nor transcription of the call will be retained by us or our third-party contractors.
By using IP Captioned Telephone Services, you agree to the transmission of the incoming audio portion of your telephone call audio to us or our agents and Automatic Speech Recognition platform(s)
THE SERVICES ARE BASED IN THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA IN THE UNITED STATES AND PROVIDED FOR ACCESS AND USE ONLY BY PERSONS LOCATED IN THE UNITED STATES.

ClearCaptions’ Telephone Number, ClearCaptions Phone and Mobile Application are intended for use in connection with the Internet Protocol Captioned Telephone Service (“IP CTS”) that ClearCaptions provides, which is a TRS product that provides captioning for telephone calls for individuals with hearing loss.

sources.title: Internet Protocol (IP) Captioned Telephone Service
quotes: Internet Protocol Captioned Telephone Service (IP CTS) is a form of telecommunications relay service (TRS) that permits an individual who can speak but who has difficulty hearing over the telephone to use a telephone and an Internet Protocol-enabled device via the Internet to simultaneously listen to the other party and read captions of what the other party is saying.
There are also versions of IP CTS that are for use with a smartphone or personal computer.

notes: ClearCaptions, LLC is the App Store seller and is listed by the FCC with full IP CTS certification at an address in Antioch, Tennessee; its terms of use say the services are based in California. The About page says ClearCaptions was founded in 2011 and separated from Purple Communications in 2017, and that it added automatic speech recognition in 2021. Android: clearcaptions.com says the app needs an iPhone or iPad, no ClearCaptions app appeared in Google Play searches for "ClearCaptions" and "ClearCaptions Mobile" (US) and guessed package names returned 404, but the terms' definition of Endpoints still says "Mobile Application for iPhone, iPad, android and tablet"; search-engine snippets mention Google Play, but no official page or Play listing was found. In-person use: no ClearCaptions page addresses captions for people in the same room; the 'No' rests on the terms (the app is intended for its IP CTS service, which captions telephone calls), the FAQ (captions during phone calls) and the tips page (only callers' words are captioned). Video calls: the FAQ answer ('only available for audio calls') is about the home ClearCaptions Phone; for the app the terms' telephone-call scope applies. Conflicts: the App Store requires iOS 15.0 while clearcaptions.com still says iOS 12.0 with a device list ending at iPhone 11; the FAQs say English only while the terms (updated November 6, 2025) mention bilingual English/Spanish users; the App Store privacy label says 'Data Not Collected' while registration collects name, date of birth, last four SSN digits, address and phone number (privacy policy and terms); the privacy policy also says ClearCaptions shares personal information for targeted advertising (website cookies). Whether call content is used to train AI is not stated. Using the app on a trip abroad is not described; the terms say the services are for people located in the US. Whether the user can choose between speech recognition and a live assistant is not stated. my.clearcaptions.com/Content/Help (General FAQs) now redirects to a JavaScript customer portal and could not be read. Pages were fetched with curl and read as text; WebFetch summaries were cross-checked against that text. The App Store lookup API returned no result for the UK, Canada, Mexico, Australia and Germany storefronts; other countries were not checked. Ratings, reviews and user counts on the store page and website were left out.
